title: Update Warehouse Stock Without Creating Stale Copies
scenario: A warehouse dashboard owns its live inventory count and display label. WarehouseDashboard::receive calls receiveShipment whenever a truck arrives, while WarehouseDashboard::labelLength calls warehouseLabelLength when the UI measures the current label.
problem_statement: WarehouseDashboard::receive calls receiveShipment, but receiveShipment currently updates only its own stockCount object, so WarehouseDashboard::stockCount still reports the old inventory after a delivery. warehouseLabelLength also creates a separate std::string object even though WarehouseDashboard::labelLength only needs to inspect the existing label. Correct the two helper declarations without changing their bodies.
constraints: Keep both function names and return types unchanged.
Do not change either function body.
learning_objective: Choose reference parameter types when a function must modify caller-owned state or inspect an existing object without creating an unnecessary copy.
instructions: Make WarehouseDashboard::receive persist each delivery in the dashboard's stored stock count, and make WarehouseDashboard::labelLength inspect the existing label without creating a redundant string object. Keep both helper function bodies unchanged.
hints: Ask whether receiveShipment should work with its own integer or with the caller's integer.
warehouseLabelLength never modifies label, but it also does not need an independent std::string object.
C++ has reference parameter forms for writable aliases and read-only aliases.
explanation: receiveShipment needs a writable lvalue reference so changes affect the caller's stock variable. warehouseLabelLength needs a const lvalue reference so it observes the existing string without copying it and cannot modify it through that parameter.
learner_goal: Make shipment updates affect the warehouse dashboard's live stock count while keeping label inspection lightweight and read-only.
